content:
mike: Heads up — we have ~12 nodes in gpu-pool-us-central1 showing NotReady/NoSchedule since ~08:10 UTC. Alert from monitoring-bot triggered.
monitoring-bot: [ALERT] node-status: gpu-pool-us-central1 node-flip: 12 nodes NotReady; avg pod evictions rising. link: https://our-monitoring/alerts/2345 :rotating_light:
anya: On it. Is this after any infra rollout?
mike: We pushed a node image kernel bump last night (image-builder v2026.02.11) to gpu pool. Logs from one of the nodes show kernel refusing the nvidia module: 
```
kernel: nvidia: module verification failed: signature and required key not available
kernel: nvidia: Unknown symbol nvidia_pci_remove (err -22)
kubelet: Device plugin registration failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to init driver: /var/log/nvidia-installer: module verification failed
```
frank: that looks like secureboot/module signature enforcement. We didn't sign the kernel module in the new image. Could be the image-builder's new kernel config enabling CONFIG_MODULE_SIG_FORCE.
jordana: Confirmed similar on two nodes. `dmesg | grep -i nvidia` shows the sigerror. Also `modinfo nvidia` is empty.
mike: Cluster-autoscaler is also misbehaving — it can't scale down because pods with PDBs are stuck on faulty nodes. That's causing capacity churn and some jobs are pending.
anya: Quick mitigation options: 1) rollback node image to previous version, 2) temporary taint nodes to prevent new scheduling and cordon+drain, 3) rebuild kernel modules with signatures (long). Which do we want to do for immediate relief?
frank: Rollback is fastest if we can replace nodes quickly. We should also avoid mass draining until we confirm autoscaler behavior (we might provoke more scale events).
jordana: I'll run a canary replacement in us-central1-a: cordon -> drain -> delete nodepool instance -> let autoscaler recreate with previous image.
mike: Also, we can patch the nodepool instance template to pin image to v2026.01.28 which had signed modules. I'll prepare infra PR.
anya: For safety I added a temporary taint to the remaining NotReady nodes to stop the scheduler from creating new pods there: `kubectl taint nodes <node> gpu-init=failing:NoSchedule` — did that for 6 nodes so far.
frank: Good call. Also need to handle the DCGM exporter / sidecars that are failing readiness probes and blocking evictions. We should set `--force` drain or evict with `--delete-local-data` where appropriate.
mike: I'll coordinate with Platform SRE to throttle cluster-autoscaler so it doesn't keep scaling up/down during the remediation window.
jordana: Canary replacement started on us-central1-a. First node replaced and comes up with image v2026.01.28, nvidia modules loaded fine. GPU pods scheduled and passing readiness.
anya: Nice. If canary is green, we should roll the rest in waves of 3 per AZ. Documenting steps in incident ticket #INC-2026-199.
mike: Created infra PR to pin image and a follow-up task to rebuild signed modules properly. Link: https://our-github/repo/pr/5432
frank: Action items: jordan a) continue canary and report, b) coordinate drains; mike: hold autoscaler; anya: update runbook with sigverify checklist; I'll own the PR review.
mike: Estimated 45m to finish full roll. Will post updates. :thumbsup:
monitoring-bot: [RESOLVE] partial: 3 nodes recovered after canary at 08:34 UTC — alert suppressed until full roll.
jordana: Canary completed across all AZs, rolling remainder now. No more sig errors observed on newly created nodes.
anya: After roll done we'll schedule follow-up to sign modules in CI and add a kernel check in image-builder pipeline to prevent this.
mike: Thanks everyone. Closing thread once roll finishes and autoscaler quiets. :white_check_mark:
